headline: Tube modelling, output limiters, a spectrum analyser and filters you shape on the graph
items: The Tube Modeller gives each output the character of one of 16 popular vacuum tubes, with drive, mix and an output stage that recreates how a valve amplifier's transformer meets a loudspeaker. Find it in the menu under Tube Modeller (Ctrl+Shift+D).

Every output now has its own brickwall limiter with adjustable threshold and release. Click the icon under an output's mute button to switch it on, or right-click it for settings. Linked outputs share their limiter settings.

A spectrum analyser shows the sound on any input or output as it plays: behind the response graph, as bars under it, and in its own window (Ctrl+Shift+A). The device does the measuring, so it works with every source, including S/PDIF, ADAT and I2S.
The Subharmonic Synthesizer adds a new octave below the bass, for recordings that are light on low end (Ctrl+Shift+S).
Filters can now be edited directly on the response graph. Drag a band's dot to change its frequency and gain, scroll to change its width, and use the card beside it to pick a shape.
Console now carries the matching firmware and installs it for you from File > Update Firmware. If a connected device runs a different version, a banner offers the update.
A setup wizard on first launch walks you through installing DSPi on a Pico. You can skip it, and run it again from Help in the menu.
Control Surfaces can now switch auxiliary outputs: a relay, lamp or amplifier trigger on a spare GPIO pin.
Dashboard cards sit in a grid that uses the width of the window. Choose Auto or one to three per row from the gear on any card.
The tool windows have been redesigned, with their controls and graphs side by side.
